request_payload.input: I want to compare two English-to-German systems on held-out online news from late 2019. Which public test set and scoring setup should I use?
request_payload.instructions: Answer the research question from existing knowledge. Aim for 180–240 words and do not exceed 300 words. Do not browse or use external tools. Do not ask a follow-up question.

output_text:
For an English-to-German comparison on late-2019 online news, use the public WMT19 general news EN-DE test set, commonly called newstest2019 or wmt19_en_de_test. It is the standard held-out benchmark from the WMT19 shared task, drawn from recent news around the WMT19 period, and it is the natural match for your data domain and date. The EN-DE test set contains roughly 3,000 sentences, large enough for a stable comparison while still allowing manual inspection of failures.

Use the official test file and reference translation, not the dev set, to avoid leakage and to allow comparison with published WMT19 results. If your systems were trained on WMT data, verify that this test set was not included in your training corpus; the WMT19 test set is held out from the shared-task training sets, but custom corpora may overlap.

For scoring, use sacreBLEU with the WMT19 official settings: case-sensitive, normalized, 4-gram BLEU. In practice, run sacreBLEU with the built-in WMT19 EN-DE test set so it applies the official tokenization and references. Report chrF or chrF2 as a secondary metric if desired, using the same tokenized inputs. Keep preprocessing identical for both systems: same tokenizer, case handling, and reference. This setup is reproducible and comparable to standard WMT19 EN-DE results.
